surfaces.part: water pool (dark teal) with grass shore around it

answer.evidence: This is a 16x16 terrain autotile mask: a dark teal water area with a lighter grass shoreline, filling the full tile (width 16 on every row). It is not a standing object. The column scan shows water at rows 0-12 with grass rows 11-15 at the bottom, which is a flat top-down ground transition with no vertical front face and no front-edge line or eave shadow. It is flat terrain seen from above, so it has no front face of 3 or more rows.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate renders as a very small swatch of dark teal with a green grass corner, not a full 4x3 ground patch, so it is hard to compare with the references at the same scale. The measured facts are favourable: 14 visible tones per tile against 3 for the grass reference, and 0% near-neutral dark edge pixels, so the edges are tinted and not a black sticker line. But 16% of the candidate is near-flat, while the grass reference has 0%. By eye, the teal body reads as a mostly flat fill with only a few shade steps (about 4) and no visible grain or tufts, where the reference grass carries clumped speckle in several greens. The grass edge is only a thin band. Because of the flat teal area and the shallow ramp, it falls short of the references, and when in doubt it fails.

Still, 16% of the candidate is near-flat, against 0% for both references. By eye, the teal water interior reads as a nearly flat fill with only about 2-3 steps. A dark teal water area sits in the upper and middle part, bordered by lighter green grass at the bottom and the left edge. The tile is a flat ground/water surface seen from above. It has no standing body, no front face and no eave or edge line, so it reads as a flat top-down tile. That is normal for terrain.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate renders much smaller than a 4x3 tile patch and reads as a dark teal water block with a thin grass rim. The measured facts look fine: 14 visible tones per tile against 3 for the grass reference, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the edges are tinted. But 16% near-flat coverage against 0% in both references matches what I see, a large, nearly uniform dark teal area with no grain, ripple or dither. The grass rim has only about 3-4 green steps, fewer than the 5-6 Beodeul uses, and shows little tuft or clump variation. By eye it is flatter and thinner than the grass reference, whose texture covers the whole surface. With so little visible and the flat water fill, I can't accept it next to the reference, and when in doubt it fails.
